title: Dataverse semantic model: what do agents know about your business data, and who tunes it?
summary: The page incorrectly says automation is not documented for the model-driven app participation setting: Microsoft documents the setting and APIs for updating app setting values. The model description and listed UI routes are supported, but the page also needs qualifications about the new configuration experience and conflicting lifecycle-management documentation.

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models lists models and associated apps or agents.
claims.quote:
select More, and if not in the More list, select Discover all, and then select Semantic models under AI section.
Associated apps or agents | Apps or agents that have access to this semantic model.

claims.claim: GET [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel lists models; include=botinfo identifies their apps and agents.
claims.quote: GET [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel?include=botinfo HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models > model > Configure > Configure table sources > Included in model > table > Remove table removes a table from model scope.
claims.quote:
Open the model and select Configure.
Under Configure table sources, select All tables to find an available table, or Included in model to review the current selection.
Search for the table display name and select the table.
Select Add table or Remove table, as appropriate.
claims.fix: Keep the route, but qualify the Configure-based UI routes with: 'These routes require the new semantic model experience; its availability depends on the environment and the documented Dataverse and solution versions.' The FAQ states that the earlier experience uses Configuration instead of Configure: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/semantic-model-faq.

POST [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel HTTP/1.1
"tables": [
    "account",
    "opportunity"
  ]

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models > model > Glossary > Add term adds glossary entries.

Open the semantic models page and select the model you want to update.

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models > model > Regenerate requests regeneration.

select Manage.
Select the environment that you want to manage.

claims.claim: Power Apps > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps controls app participation.
claims.quote:
select Apps.
Find the app that you want to manage, and then select Edit.

claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model signal settings regeneration API dvtablesearch entity reference; semantic model regeneration API PowerShell. claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model regeneration API PowerShell regenerate action signals configuration. Read regenerate-semantic-model, manage-semantic-models and webapi/reference/dvtablesearch; results documented the UI and scheduled regeneration, not a regeneration call.

claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment setting Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell; Work IQ Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment API; Dataverse intelligence organization API enabled settings. claims.where: controls[7].api; Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for the model-driven app Work IQ participation setting.
claims.quote:
Creates or updates app/organization level override.
AppUniqueName: Model-driven app unique name (Optional).
SettingName: Setting definition unique name (Required).
Value: Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).
claims.fix: Replace controls[7].api with REST 'POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/savesettingvalue. Note that SettingName identifies m365copilotmodelappenabled, Value supplies its override, and AppUniqueName targets the app. The setting identifier is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/user/use-business-apps-work-iq; the general setting-value API at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/get-update-setting-value-using-code and POST action convention at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/use-web-api-actions establish the operation. Cite these pages and narrow the prose absence to signal and regeneration settings and the environment and tenant Work IQ switches.

claims.claim: The Dataverse semantic model gives agents and Copilot a shared business-aware understanding of Dataverse data.
claims.quote: The Dataverse semantic model gives AI agents and Copilot experiences a shared, business-aware understanding of your Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Makers and administrators tune table sources, signals and glossary terms.
claims.quote: Makers and administrators can then fine-tune each model's table sources and signals, and add domain-specific glossary terms for business language that automatic extraction can't infer.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Table selection and signals do not override Dataverse security roles or table, column and record access controls.
claims.quote: They don't override or replace Dataverse security roles, table-, column-, or record-level access controls, or application-level configurations.

claims.claim: The platform automatically provisions models for supported Dataverse Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: The platform automatically provisions semantic models for supported Copilot experiences over Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Data scope is the set of covered Dataverse tables with semantic indexing applied over them.
claims.quote: The data scope defines the set of Dataverse tables covered by the semantic model. Semantic indexing is applied over those tables

claims.claim: Inferred signals include relationships, public and sub-grid views, form summaries, table summaries and optional sample rows.
claims.quote:
Table relationships
Public views with join conditions and sub-grid views that define which records and columns are relevant for a scenario.
Forms summaries
Table summaries
Sample data rows
claims.fix: Change 'public and sub-grid views' in the building-block table to 'public views with join conditions and sub-grid views', retaining the documented qualification.

claims.claim: The glossary supplies terms, acronyms and definitions that inferred signals cannot infer.
claims.quote: The glossary allows makers to add domain-specific terms, acronyms, synonyms, and definitions that system signals can't infer.

claims.claim: Enabling Dataverse intelligence automatically provisions the model.
claims.quote: Once Dataverse intelligence is enabled, the semantic model is provisioned automatically.

claims.claim: The model regenerates automatically every 12 hours.
claims.quote: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours to reflect schema changes.

claims.claim: Initial generation can take up to two hours.
claims.quote: Initial generation can take up to two hours

claims.claim: Dataverse intelligence is now part of Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Dataverse intelligence is now part of Business Applications in Work IQ.

claims.claim: Copilot in Power Apps consumes Dataverse semantic models.
claims.quote:
The semantic model is automatically consumed by the following experiences:
Copilot in Power Apps

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse consumes Dataverse semantic models.
claims.quote:
The semantic model is automatically consumed by the following experiences:
Copilot in Power Apps
Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse

claims.claim: Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 consumes Dataverse semantic models.
claims.quote: Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 — Uses Dataverse data to power sales scenarios.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents with Dataverse tables as knowledge consume the models.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse data — Agents built in Copilot Studio that use Dataverse tables as a knowledge source.

claims.claim: A model's name reflects the source that provisioned it.
claims.quote: Semantic models are named based on the source that provisioned them.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Changes to a shared model's signals, table controls or glossary apply to all experiences associated with that model.
claims.quote: If multiple apps or agents share the same semantic model (for example, Sales Agent and Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales both use SalesSpecificQnA), changes to that model apply to all experiences associated with it.

claims.where: What it is: Custom models; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Custom model creation is a preview feature.
claims.quote:
Create a custom semantic model (preview)
This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Custom models can serve a specific purpose through direct API and action calls.
claims.quote: You can also create a custom model for a specific purpose. Custom models are currently usable through direct API and action calls

claims.claim: Creating a custom model does not automatically associate it with an app or agent.
claims.quote: creation doesn't automatically associate a model with an app or agent.

claims.where: What it is: The other meaning
claims.claim: Fabric Power BI semantic models describe an analytical domain using metrics and business-friendly terminology.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Fabric, Power BI semantic models are a logical description of an analytical domain, with metrics, business friendly terminology, and representation, to enable deeper analysis.

claims.where: What it is: The other meaning
claims.claim: Fabric and Power BI manage separate analytical semantic-model objects.
claims.quote: Semantic models are independent items in Fabric and can be managed via REST APIs to enumerate semantic models in a workspace, check for dependencies (reports/dashboards) and model content, and delete unused ones.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: The default-on rule excepts EU/EFTA, government-related and nonproduction environments.
claims.quote:
The following environments are exceptions:
European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments
Government-related environments
Nonproduction environments

claims.claim: Semantic modeling is one of the capabilities enabled by Work IQ.
claims.quote:
When Work IQ is on, a new environment can use the following capabilities:
Search Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data by using Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in-app and mainline search.
Semantic modeling.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence requirement or price specific to the semantic model.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model license pricing storage; semantic model licensing Dataverse. Read semantic-model-overview, fine-tune-semantic-model-signals, understand-costs and Work IQ api-overview. Consumer/API billing is documented, but no separate semantic-model licence or price.

claims.claim: Semantic modeling is among Work IQ features that use extra search-index storage.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: All Dataverse indexes are reported at the Dataverse database capacity rate.
claims.quote: All Dataverse indexes are reported at the Dataverse database capacity rate.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Storage; What to check
claims.claim: Dataverse search storage appears as DataverseSearch at environment level in capacity reporting.
claims.quote: Storage consumed by Dataverse search is reported at the environment level as a table called DataverseSearch. It was previously named RelevanceSearch.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ costs follow the consuming experience, whose spending policy Microsoft says to configure.
claims.quote:
For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.
Configure the policy for the consuming experience rather than looking for a separate business applications spending policy.

claims.quote: Removing a table from the model doesn't delete the Dataverse table.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not instant; controls[4].note

claims.quote: Saving configuration and regenerating the model are separate operations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not instant; controls[4].note

claims.claim: Regeneration runs across all semantic models in the environment.
claims.quote: Regeneration runs across all semantic models in the environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Generated content is read-only

claims.quote:
Generated summaries, views, and relationships are read-only.
you can't directly edit the generated content.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risks and limits: Sample data rows
claims.claim: Sample table rows is off by default.
claims.quote: The Sample table rows signal is turned off by default.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Sample data rows
claims.claim: When enabled, the sample-row signal uses selected row values as context for agents.
claims.quote: When available and enabled, it uses a selection of row values to give agents context about the table's content.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No environment copy or move
claims.claim: Semantic models do not support environment copy or move.
claims.quote: The semantic model currently doesn't support environment copy or move operations. After any environment copy or move, turn Dataverse Intelligence off and back on in the Power Platform Admin Center to force a restart.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket statement with: 'The overview documents no support for environment copy or move and advises restarting Dataverse Intelligence afterwards. The configuration article also says semantic models are solution-aware and that their configuration can move between environments in solutions.' Both pages are already cited; the second is https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/fine-tune-semantic-model-signals#add-semantic-model-to-a-solution.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No environment copy or move
claims.claim: Models whose names contain Secondary_model do not carry over with environment copy or move.
claims.quote: Secondary_model is a naming convention that indicates the semantic model isn't ALM-compatible. If you see this term in a model name, the model doesn't carry over when you copy or move the environment.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is unavailable in sovereign and government clouds including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.quote: Verify who holds System Administrator or the Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker roles.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review capacity reporting without a matching control row.

claims.where: Governance controls: Roles; What to check
claims.claim: Managing a semantic model requires System Administrator or the combination of Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.
claims.quote:
You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model:
System Administrator -or-
Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.

claims.claim: Power Platform administrators manage Work IQ settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to manage settings and assign other roles.

claims.claim: The environment-level Work IQ setting requires an environment administrator account.
claims.quote: Use the environment-level setting to manage business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. You need an environment administrator account.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center audience setting requires a tenant administrator account.
claims.quote: Use the tenant-level setting to manage whether Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data can be used in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat across the tenant. You need a tenant administrator account.

claims.claim: The app-level participation setting requires a maker account.
claims.quote: Use the app-level setting to manage whether a model-driven app's tables, forms, and views are available in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research in Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Agent Builder. You need a maker account.

claims.claim: All users is the default tenant audience option.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default.

claims.claim: The tenant audience options are No users, All users and Specific groups.
claims.quote:
To turn off access for everyone, select No users.
To turn on access for everyone, select All users.
To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups, and then add or remove groups.

claims.claim: App participation changes must be saved and published.
claims.quote:
Set Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps to On or Off.
Select Save.
Select Publish.

claims.claim: System-defined glossary entries can be edited.
claims.quote: You can edit them to better reflect your organization's terminology

claims.claim: System-defined glossary entries cannot be deleted.
claims.quote: The Delete action is disabled for system-defined entries.

select the table, open Table signals, and turn the signal off.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Model-wide signal settings take precedence over per-table settings.
claims.quote: A model-wide signal setting takes precedence over per-table settings.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Managing individual views and relationships requires the corresponding signal enabled at both model and table levels.
claims.quote: In Configure, turn the signal on under Manage signals, then turn it on for the included table under Table signals. To manage individual views or relationships, the corresponding signal must be enabled at both levels.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Turning off the tenant setting blocks Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse data sharing even for an app configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Turning off environment Work IQ makes semantic modeling unavailable there.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.where: Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: Participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data; Microsoft directs administrators to App Access controls.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: Microsoft's semantic model articles do not list audit events for table, signal or glossary changes.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model license pricing storage audit events table signals glossary changes; semantic model audit Dataverse. Read overview, FAQ, signals, glossary and regeneration; no model-change events listed. General Dataverse audit excerpts did not identify these changes.
